thread:
Maya: Heads-up — Opero just came back with a list of asks for their pilot. They're asking for reserved capacity + burst credits, per-route throughput guarantees, and an SLA credit clause. Need quick call to decide packaging and an escape hatch.
Sam: They sign faster if we reduce upfront commit and add a predictable add-on. willing to give 30% discount on a 6mo commit.
Jen: Curious what Opero's expected QPS and SLO shape is. we need concrete gating metrics before we promise per-route guarantees.
Maya: Sales says ~400 qps peak, steady 50 qps, latency target p50 < 80ms, p95 < 350ms. pilot is 90 days.
Kevin: 400 qps peak with p95 <350ms is doable but depends on model choice & batch settings. per-route throughput means routing isolation — that costs reserved GPU headroom.
Alex: Legal — if we add SLA credits we need precise definitions for downtime and credit calc. also want a clear escape hatch if model drift causes quality regressions.
Olivia: Finance — what's the revenue profile for a discounted 6mo commit w/ burst top-up? need ARR vs cash and whether we classify burst as usage or pre-paid credits.
Sam: Proposal from my side: Offer a 'Pilot Reserved Pack' (2 reserved lanes) + 150k burst credits, with an optional priority-lane add-on billed monthly. Keep commit low to reduce friction.
Maya: I sketched three packaging options:
- Option A: Pilot Reserved Pack (2 lanes) + 150k burst, soft SLA (service credit up to 5% of monthly bill). 6mo commit, 30% discount.
- Option B: On-demand + priority-lane addon (no commit), burst pay-as-you-go, no SLA credit but guaranteed routing priority during business hours.
- Option C: Dedicated trial (4 lanes) small commit, strict SLA (99.9) + higher price, auto-fallback to on-demand if capacity constrained.
Sam: Option A seems easiest to close. Option B is safer operationally. Option C is big ask.
Jen: For launch gates we should require: 1) 3 successful integrations, 2) performance within SLO for 2 weeks, 3) cost/unit <= target. If any fail, we rollback routing guarantees.
Kevin: Implementation notes: we need autoscale headroom + config to throttle burst via token bucket. also KV cache warmup will strongly affect peak latencies. recommend prefilling cache during pilot ramp.
Maya: Good. Also need a contract escape: if model QPS causes >3 regressions in quality metrics (we'll define eval set) within pilot then routing downgrades automatically. Alex ok with that?
Alex: Yes, but define 'regression' and threshold now. propose >2% drop in LLM eval score on agreed prompt set over a 7-day window.
Olivia: We should treat burst credits as prepaid liability on the balance sheet. If customer doesn't use them, apply standard expiration after pilot end.
Sam: I'll negotiate to keep burst expiry 30 days post-pilot.
Maya: ops-bot created ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2178 (Pilot: Opero) :point_up:
ops-bot: Ticket INF-2178 created and assigned to @Kevin and @Maya.
Kevin: I'll allocate a dedicated queue and test KV prefill script. ETA to get a perf baseline is 4 dev days.
Jen: I'll draft launch gate checklist and an eval prompt set.
Olivia: I'll model pricing scenarios and post numbers in the ticket by EOD Thursday.
Sam: I'll confirm customer's commitment level and push for Option A.
Maya: Meeting to finalize: tomorrow 10:30 PT. Action owners: Kevin (infra baseline + scripts), Jen (gates + evals), Olivia (pricing P&L), Sam (customer negotiation). We'll circle after perf baseline. :thumbsup:
Kevin: noted.
Alex: I'll draft SLA wording and the regression clause.
Maya: Thanks all — aim to have a go/no-go decision by the end of next week.
